topic: FXRP reserve-control architecture, escrow conditions, supply history and XRPL.to data-use constraints

sources.supports: Current supply, backing, Core Vault, six agents, escrow count and holder concentrations.

Nine reserve/fee/custodian addresses, shared Core Vault, six agents, escrow recipients/conditions, historical escrow ladder, agent mint concentration, wallet distribution and FXRP totalSupply history.
sources.limits: Historical ledger snapshot; current contract permissions and escrow dates require revalidation.

sources.usage: Future ingestion must use documented API, not scrape or copy XRPL.to UI; preserve visible attribution/link.

findings.shared_pool: All six agents can draw from the shared Core Vault, per historical fixed-ledger analysis.
findings.trigger_authority: Historical analysis reports one designated account under the Flare governance contract can trigger Core Vault transfers; do not identify this with a human or assume current mapping without contract verification.

interpretation: Most backing is concentrated in a shared Core Vault; the six agents are not six independent backing pools.

The Core Vault is accessible to agents, but the historical analysis reports a designated trigger-account permission for transfers and a common escrow payout destination. Current permission mapping remains unverified.
The 140M escrow total is a rolling-liquidity mechanism, not a permanent lock; the historical 14x10M ladder had daily expiries, but the current escrow dates must be fetched from XRPL account_objects.
Current supply remains below the June 1 peak; the August 30 independent series shows minting had slowed sharply. This is counter-evidence to unqualified claims of accelerating adoption.

The historical median of 10 XRP across non-exchange wallets suggests retail-sized usage in that sample; it does not establish the beneficial-owner profile of all FXRP supply or institutional treasury balances.
restrictions: XRPL.to explicitly directs automated clients to its documented API and prohibits scraping, reverse engineering or copying its UI. Use https://api.xrpl.to/v1 and preserve attribution/link.
